        it waits in the queue.

from /scope/harness-integration import HarnessIntegrationScope
from /scope/project-data import ProjectDataScope
from /scope/prompt-mode import PromptEditor
from /scope/prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/message-list import MessageList
from /scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts import ModeSystemPromptsScope
from /scope/prompt-mode/modes import PromptModesScope
from /scope/spec-build import SpecBuildScope

export scope PromptSendingScope:
    concept: {PromptSendingConcept}

concept PromptSendingConcept:
    pitch:
        How a prompt gets to the harness, whether written in the chat input or
        sent on the application's behalf.

    shape: {PromptSendingShape}

shape PromptSendingShape:
    description:
        A prompt is sent in one of the @{PromptModesScope}, with anything
        attached to it. Sending is never blocked by the harness working.

    tasks:
        A task, a prompt in Code, Chain, Spec, or Freeform, is sent straight away while
        the harness is free. While the harness is working, it waits in the
        @{PromptEditor}'s queue instead, in the order it was sent, keeping its
        mode and attachments, until its turn comes.

        When a task is actually sent, the spec is built ahead of it, as the
        @{SpecBuildScope} says, the task showing "Building" until the build is
        over; then its hidden anchor is compiled and run. It heads the
        @{MessageList} as the latest task, and is saved in the prompt history,
        as the @{ProjectDataScope} says. A prompt that fails to compile or run
        fails its task, and doesn't stop the queue.

    questions:
        A question, a prompt in Ask, never queues: it runs straight away, even
        while the harness is working on a task or other questions, joins the
        questions stacked above the @{ChatInputScope}'s tabs, and is saved
        among the questions asked.

    sendingToATask:
        While a task is running, more can be sent to it, as to a terminal
        session, from the @{ChatInputScope}'s "Send to task", as it says. What
        is sent is written as a hidden anchor and compiled like any prompt,
        unless the task was sent from Freeform, when it goes just as it was
        typed, with its attachments, its
        references, attachments, and Slice toggle included, so it can reference
        the spec, but the spec isn't built first, and its systemPrompt isn't
        sent, since the run already has the one it began with. It goes to the
        running task's run as a message of its own, as the
        @{HarnessIntegrationScope} says, and is not a task of its own: it
        doesn't head the @{MessageList}, isn't among the previous tasks, and
        can't be resent. It is shown in the task's output and kept with its
        record, as the @{PromptEditor} says. A message that fails to compile
        isn't sent, and a notification titled "Could not send to the task" says
        why, what was typed going back into the input. A message whose task
        ends before it can be sent is queued instead, as a task, so nothing
        typed is lost.

    onTheApplicationsBehalf:
        Something in the application can send a prompt as if it were written in
        the chat input and sent from one of its tabs. It goes just the same
        way: queued if the harness is busy, shown as a task, and entered in the
        history. What is being written in the chat input, and attached to it,
        is left alone.

    resending:
        A prompt sent before can be sent again, from a Resend button: a small
        ghost button with a rotating-arrow icon, whose tooltip says it sends
        the prompt again as it was sent. It sits at the right of the latest
        task's header, and of the heading of each previous task and previous
        answer, beside its chevron; clicking it never opens or closes the item.

        Resending sends the prompt as it was typed, in the mode it was sent in,
        with the text that was attached to it, and sliced or not as it was, as
        though it were sent afresh from the chat input: a task queues while the
        harness is working, a question runs straight away, and either is
        compiled anew, against the spec and system prompt as they are now,
        building the spec first as any task does, and saved in the history as a
        new task or question. The prompt resent stays where it is. A prompt
        whose mode isn't known, saved before modes were, is resent from the
        chat input's selected tab. What is being written in the chat input, and
        attached to it, is left alone, and so is the Slice toggle.

    cancelling:
        The task under way can be cancelled, from a Cancel button: a small
        ghost button with a stop icon, whose tooltip says "Cancel this task",
        at the right of the latest task's header, beside its Resend button,
        shown only while the task is building, compiling, or running. A task
        is cancelled straight away, whatever the harness is in the middle of:
        a build or compile under way is abandoned before the task is run, and
        a run is stopped, the harness's process ended, not left to finish its
        turn.

        A cancelled task keeps the output it had so far, and its status reads
        "Cancelled", as the @{MessageList} shows, in the history as much as in
        its header. It adds no commit note, and any change the harness had
        already made to files is left as it is. The queue carries on after it,
        as it does after a task that fails, sending the next prompt waiting in
        it, and the next task carries on the same conversation. Questions are
        not cancelled with it.

    sendingToTheOtherMode:
        A task sent in Code alone can be sent to Spec, and one sent in Spec
        alone can be sent to Code, from a small ghost button beside its Resend
        button, tinted the colour of the mode it sends to, whose tooltip says
        "Send to Spec" or "Send to Code". It sits wherever Resend does for a
        task, at the right of the latest task's header and of the heading of
        each previous task, and clicking it never opens or closes the item.
        Tasks sent in Chain, questions, and prompts whose mode isn't known
        don't offer it.

        Sending to the other mode is resending, as above, in every way but the
        mode: the prompt is sent in the other mode, with that mode's system
        prompt, and saved in the history as a new task in that mode.

---

The spec says the opposite in several places:

If I built separate Code and Spec sessions that run in parallel, the code would stop matching all four of these. So the spec needs to change first, in a Spec session. It would need to say:

1. **Modes and harness integration:** Code tasks and Spec tasks each keep their own conversation, and when the project is opened each resumes its latest one.
2. **Running at once:** a Code task and a Spec task can run at the same time. Tasks in the same mode still run one at a time.
3. **Queue:** either one queue per mode, or one shared queue that sends the next task whose mode is free. This matters because `queue-list` was just split out and the shared "Send next" and auto-send switch assume one line of tasks.
4. **Chain and Freeform:** which conversation each uses and what it waits for. Chain runs Spec then Code steps, so it probably needs both modes free.
5. **Session controls:** the context figure and New conversation apply to the selected tab's own conversation.
